title: Matrix input and grading
text: A matrix question can ask for one particular matrix, any basis of a space, or any matrix with a stated property. Choose the mathematical test first; the editor collects entries, while the answer test and response tree decide correctness and marks. Try the matrix questions before adapting one.

title: Matrix input and grading
text:
For teachers

Decisions for a question author



What the prompt asks
Appropriate check
Teacher value in the PRT




A particular matrix
AlgEquiv compares dimensions and corresponding entries; EqualComAss also checks written form.
The expected matrix.


Any basis of a null, column or row space
IsBasis checks membership, independence and completeness.
The original matrix \(A\), with nullspace, columnspace or rowspace selected.


Integer entries, a given determinant or nonidentity
Separate MatrixProperty nodes can give separate marks.
The expected property result: true, an exact determinant such as 1, or false.


Another condition, such as symmetric positive definiteness
A named PythonChecker function in an author file.
The value the function needs, such as true for the SPD example.



An entry-by-entry check would reject many correct answers to “give any basis” or “give any matrix satisfying these conditions.” See Python answer tests for the choice and the complete SPD authoring walkthrough for a custom rule. An equivalent native Moodle STACK question needs corresponding Maxima checks; these Python test names are specific to this port.
If the shape is part of the task, let learners choose a bounded number of columns for null or column-space bases, or rows for row-space bases. An empty basis cannot currently be entered because the editor needs positive dimensions. For a fixed-size task, the model answer determines the editor’s shape. The built-in IsBasis and MatrixProperty tests require exact rational entries (integers or fractions). An author-supplied PythonChecker can choose another domain within the input limits. Set any partial credit in the response trees; neither correct cells nor green basis vectors earn marks by themselves.


What learners see
A learner fills matrix cells, presses Validate answers to inspect the interpreted matrix, then presses Check answer. Empty cells are invalid. The editor retains typed forms such as x+x or 1/2; resizing keeps cells that still fit and leaves new cells blank. Editing, resizing, resetting or switching variants clears an earlier result and requires validation again. After an IsBasis check, vector colors explain membership and dependence, but the response tree still determines the score.

title: Question corpus
Question corpus
text:
For developers

Authored test mismatches
These cases disagree with expectations authored in the XML and are kept out of the interactive gallery. Reviewed causes are named below; an authored-test mismatch alone does not identify whether the cause is the port or the original question. The baseline JSON retains the exact expected and observed results.

AlgMap-8.10
Upstream authoring bug in the PRT. At the failing variant, a=8, b=9, c=2, and d=3, so the correct answer is 8*(t+y)/2 + 9*(t+y)/3 = 7*(t+y). Both authored model answers therefore have no fraction operator. The only full-credit branch requires SingleFrac, which rejects this product; every later branch awards zero. Authored tests 1 and 2 nevertheless expect full credit. The pinned native STACK test also rejects 7*(t+y) under SingleFrac. The port’s random choices expose a latent assumption in the original question; this diagnosis uses the fixed values above, rather than assuming Maxima generates those values for the same seed.
Algebra Refresher / 08 Algebraic fractions · 2 failed of 12 replayed seed/case combinations. For seed 1856951054, case 1, input ans = (7*(t + y)): prt1 expected score 1.0 and answer note 1-0-T, but produced score 0.0 and answer note 1-0-F | 1-1-F.

title: STACK questions with AI Feedback
text:
Bring selected Moodle STACK questions to a teaching website. Learners practise in their browser, see how their answers are interpreted, and can request guided AI Feedback alongside the question’s mathematical grading. The exported XML, scoring rules and author tests remain available for inspection.
Quarto turns plain-text teaching material into web pages. STACK SymPy adds interactive question cards to those pages for publication as a static site.

title: Authoring and support
Authoring and support
text:
For developers

Question-block options
All options below are written as #| key: value inside a .stack-question block. File paths are relative to the containing .qmd page.








Option
Default or requirement
Purpose




file
Required
XML filename.


question
Required
Exact XML question name.


seed
1; signed 32-bit integer
Starting seed for repeatable variants.


variants
1; from 1 to 20
Number of variants prepared at build time.


review
false
Show Run question tests for the selected variant.


diagnostics
false
Display build errors while authoring.


feedback
false
Enable the separately installed AI Feedback extension.


context
auto
Nearby prose, none, or comma-separated context IDs.


feedback-language
Document lang
Language for AI explanations.


feedback-policy
Inherited policy
Name of a policy loaded by the shared feedback extension.


label
Generated card ID
Stable exercise key for policy overrides. A Quarto block ID also identifies a card.


python-checkers
Omitted
Python filename read during the build; register named functions in CHECKERS. No source manifest is required.



The base extension requires Python 3.11+, SymPy 1.13.3, Quarto 1.4+ and HTML output with JavaScript. AI Feedback requires version 0.8.0+ of that extension and Quarto 1.8.27+. Set STACK_SYMPY_PYTHON to the Python interpreter to use when Quarto’s default interpreter is not the required environment.


Input and XML reference
The source is a Moodle STACK <quiz> containing named <question type="stack"> entries. Category and description entries are skipped. Retain inputs, PRTs, deployed seeds and <qtest> cases. Unsupported fields and HTML/CASText fail with a question-specific location.



XML input setting
Handling




type
algebraic, scalar numerical, or rectangular matrix.


tans
The input’s model answer. A PRT node’s tans is a separate test argument.


strictsyntax, insertstars
Strict syntax is required. Insertion mode 0 requires explicit *; mode 1 also accepts adjacent products.


forbidwords, forbidfloat
Reject configured words or decimal literals.


requirelowestterms
Reject reducible written integer fractions during validation.


checkanswertype
Check the supported STACK applicability/type rule; this is not a full shape or equality check.


mustverify, showvalidation
Verification metadata and preview visibility are retained; this UI always requires validation before grading. Supported visibility values are 0, 1, 3.


syntaxhint, boxsize
Parse the authored hint and size text fields within the supported limits.


matrix
Optional fixed/resizable dimension settings; see matrix input.



allowwords and input options must be empty; nondefault syntax attributes and other insertion modes are unsupported. Question-level assumereal and assumepositive affect symbolic assumptions. questionsimplify=0 preserves supported written forms when they survive variant preparation; unsupported held expressions fail clearly.
CASText supports {@expression@} for scalars, collections and matrices, and {@left=right@} for a displayed scalar equality. The placeholders [[input:name]], [[validation:name]] and [[feedback:name]] connect the question text to inputs and response trees. HTML is sanitized. This does not provide arbitrary Maxima evaluation or all STACK text directives.


Answer entry and form
Supported scalar notation includes arithmetic + - * / ^ (also **), parentheses, symbols and the constants %pi, %e, %i. Functions are sqrt, sin, cos, tan, sec, csc, cot, sinh, cosh, tanh, sech, csch, coth, exp, log, abs, rational-polynomial gcd and real scalar mod. Aliases are ln, cosec, cosech. mod(x,0)=x follows Maxima’s convention. With insertion mode 1, 2x, 2(x+1) and (x+1)(x-1) are products; xy remains one symbol and spaces alone never imply multiplication.
Form tests EqualComAss, FacForm, SingleFrac, LowestTerms require a direct input name in sans. EqualComAss preserves structure up to commutative and associative reordering. FacForm requires one polynomial variable in testoptions and handles univariate rational polynomials. SingleFrac checks an equivalent single written fraction or atomic answer. LowestTerms checks written integer fractions and supported denominator restrictions, without comparing the teacher value or cancelling symbolic polynomial factors.
NumAbsolute and NumRelative use the configured tolerance; omitted or syntactically malformed options default to 0.05. NumDecPlaces requires an explicit count from 1 to 50 and checks trailing zeros as written precision. Use a numerical answer test for an approximate measurement rather than treating algebraic equivalence as a tolerance test.


Lists, sets and equations
Lists use [...]; sets use {...}. Both may nest and be empty. Limits are 32 entries per container, six collection levels and 128 total collection nodes, with scalar expression leaves. List comparison is ordered. Set comparison normalizes members without a general proof of every possible scalar identity; see set conventions. Sets explains outer duplicates and missing/extra members. EqualComAss retains list order, nested boundaries and repeated set entries. SameType follows applicability: two sets have the same type, and different-length lists can have the same type. It does not establish equality.
Use exact fractions in sets and prepared author collections. Direct decimal list entries have narrower support: literal constant arithmetic with integer powers works; decimal-bearing functions, symbolic terms, transformed collections and transitive author aliases do not. Collection tests require a direct learner input, preserving the literal arithmetic used by the comparison.
AlgEquiv also supports Boolean constants and and, or, not, implies, xor, xnor, with nounand, nounor, nounnot aliases and at most eight Boolean variables. Supported polynomial equations and their disjunctions use a product-of-residuals rule: a=0 or b=0 matches a*b=0. Root multiplicity is retained. Conjunctions/negations of equations, variable denominators and mixtures of equations with Boolean propositions are unsupported. Principal complex roots and logarithms require attention to their domains; the conventions reference records the known differences and proof limits.


Author variables and helpers
Write assignments as name:expression;; list indexing is 1-based. In addition to the scalar functions above, authors can use:







Purpose
Supported helpers




Variants
rand, rand_with_step.


Scalar algebra/calculus
diff, expand, factor, ratsimp, cancel, ev(expr), ev(expr,simp), num, denom, integer lcm.


Decimal/significant-figure display
decimalplaces, dispdp, displaydp, significantfigures, dispsf.


Finite collections
set, setify, listify, union, intersection, setdifference, member, subsetp, cardinality.


Model basis generation
nullspace_basis, columnspace_basis, rowspace_basis. The basis checker still receives the original matrix.



ratsimp preserves a supported common-denominator form. listify(list) keeps order; sorting a set with listify supports rational scalar members only. Finite helpers require normal simplification and exact fractions. Prepare their results in question variables before using form-sensitive collection tests; helper feedback variables and held helper execution are unsupported. float is recognized, but floating-point author values cannot be stored in prepared variants and are rejected. Learners cannot call author-only helpers.


Policy configuration
Loading definitions with policy-files or page-policy-files does not select a policy. Select project-policy or page-policy explicitly; STACK uses the shared math-exercise policy namespace. This site’s configuration is:
ai-feedback:
  policy-files: feedback/course.yml
  project-policy:
    math-exercise: course-mathematics
A named policy can inherit settings and replace its hint sequence:
ai-feedback:
  policies:
    course-mathematics:
      max-words: 120
      reset-on-run: true
    brief-mathematics:
      extends: course-mathematics
      max-words: 90
    two-step-practice:
      extends: brief-mathematics
      steps:
        - step-prompt: Ask one guiding question without giving a formula or answer.
        - step-prompt: Give a concise worked explanation of this task.
          allow-full-solution: true
Place this definition in a policy YAML file and select feedback-policy: two-step-practice on a card. A stable label targets exercises.math-exercise overrides. The policy resolver applies defaults, project/page selections, exercise overrides, the selected policy and its ancestry, then the current step. steps replaces the inherited list; base-prompt supplies ongoing instructions and step-prompt one step. The retired prompt, inline integrations and inline defaults settings are rejected. See the shared policy reference.
Edits cancel stale responses and clear grading evidence while retaining hint progress. Check resets hints by default; reset-on-run: false preserves progress. Changing variants always resets hints. Only a displayed reply or a generated copy prompt advances the step. .ai-feedback-context and .math-exercise-context are aliases of .ai-context. Explicit jsxgraph:diagram-id references can include visual context through the shared extension; diagrams are not collected implicitly.


Tests, runtime and contribution
PRTs are acyclic response-tree graphs with =, +, - branch score operations, feedback, notes and weighted aggregation. Branch-specific penalties are not supported. Native <qtest> cases check scores, initial-attempt penalty and ordered answer notes, including anchored notes and NULL. The browser has no Moodle attempt state. For custom predicates, also select the checker filename on CLI tests; see the Python guide.
The same Python core runs locally and in a Pyodide worker. Quarto prepares variants at build time; the worker validates, grades and replays tests. A worker timeout can stop runaway grading. The native comparison and project regression report provide separate evidence, not a blanket compatibility claim. These reports are generated by CI; a normal quarto render does not rerun their mathematical comparisons.
For a source checkout, install requirements-dev.txt, run PYTHONPATH=_extensions/stack-sympy python -m pytest -q tests, check the runtime bundle with python scripts/bundle_runtime.py --check, and consult the development guide for browser/native checks. Include a minimal XML question and its qtests when reporting a grading issue. General matrix arithmetic, inequalities, units, arbitrary Maxima scripts and Moodle’s full attempt workflow remain unsupported.

title: Python answer tests
text: A question may have many mathematically correct answers. This guide helps you choose a test for a space or property and shows how ordinary STACK response trees (PRTs) continue to award the marks. The worked questions let you try each choice.

title: Python answer tests
text:
For teachers

Choose the mathematical test








Task
Test
What counts as correct




Give this particular matrix
AlgEquiv
Corresponding entries are equivalent and dimensions agree.


Give any basis of a matrix’s null, column or row space
IsBasis
Independent vectors span that space, regardless of the particular basis chosen.


Give any basis of a space specified by basis vectors
IsBasis
Independent vectors have the same span as the reference vectors.


Give a matrix satisfying the built-in conditions
MatrixProperty
Integer entries, a stated determinant or identity status.


Give a matrix satisfying another condition
PythonChecker
A named author function checks the stated property, such as symmetric positive definiteness.



AlgEquiv is an existing STACK answer-test name. IsBasis, MatrixProperty and PythonChecker are Python additions to this port. They keep STACK-style inputs and PRT scoring, but a native Moodle STACK question needs equivalent Maxima tests and may need different matrix-input settings.


Basis questions: use the matrix in the question
If the prompt asks for a basis of \(\ker A\), the PRT compares the learner’s proposed vectors against the original matrix \(A\), not against one precomputed list of basis vectors. Choose nullspace; use columnspace or rowspace for the other two spaces. The input’s model answer can be generated from \(A\) with the matching author helper. Another independent basis is still correct. For example, if \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\end{pmatrix}\), both the columns of \(\begin{pmatrix}-2&-3\\1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\) and those of \(\begin{pmatrix}-5&-1\\1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\) span \(\ker A\).








IsBasis option
Space being checked
How learners enter vectors




nullspace
Null space of the original \(A\)
One vector per column


columnspace
Column space of the original \(A\)
One vector per column


rowspace
Row space of the original \(A\)
One vector per row


columns (default)
Span of independent reference columns supplied by the author
One vector per column


rows
Span of independent reference rows supplied by the author
One vector per row



The older columns and rows modes answer a different question: they compare spans with a supplied reference basis. Use them when that basis really defines the space in the prompt. For a matrix-defined space, use the original-matrix options above. The basis examples show alternate correct responses and learner-selected column counts. The matrix editor cannot represent an empty basis, so choose a task with a nonzero-dimensional answer space.
After checking a basis, green marks a nonzero vector in the target space when the valid submitted vectors are independent; it can still belong to an incomplete family. Yellow marks a dependent valid family and red marks zero or out-of-space vectors. These colors explain the answer; the PRT awards marks only for the complete basis in the examples. Edits and resizing clear the colors.


Matrix conditions and partial credit
The determinant-one task accepts any integer \(2\times2\) matrix with determinant \(1\) except the identity. Three PRTs give one third of the score each: integer entries, determinant and nonidentity. An entry-by-entry comparison with the model would reject other correct matrices.








MatrixProperty option
Expected result supplied in PRT tans
Condition




integer_entries
true or false
Are all entries integers?


determinant
An exact rational value such as 1
Does this square matrix have that determinant?


identity
true or false
Is it the identity matrix?



The PRT’s tans is the expected property result, not the matrix in the prompt. For determinant one it is 1; for nonidentity it is false. MatrixProperty covers these three conditions only. A different condition calls for PythonChecker or an equivalent native STACK author calculation.


Symmetric positive definite matrices
Try giving any symmetric positive definite \(2\times2\) matrix with integer or exact-fraction entries. For a real symmetric matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}\), Sylvester’s criterion says \(a>0\) and \(ac-b^2>0\). The identity works, as does \(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\). A symmetric matrix with determinant zero does not work.
This uses an author-supplied PythonChecker: positive definiteness is not a built-in MatrixProperty option. The checker receives the parsed matrix and the expected result true; the PRT awards credit. Explore the live question, then follow the single authoring walkthrough to see its complete Python file, XML node, Quarto block and tests.
Variant Variant 1Give any symmetric positive definite \(2\times2\) matrix. Use integers or exact fractions.  Validate answersCheck answerRun question testsShow source```{.stack-question #docs-spd-matrix}
#| file: ../questions/symmetric-positive-definite.xml
#| question: A symmetric positive definite matrix
#| python-checkers: ../questions/spd-checker.py
#| review: true
```Show STACK source<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!-- Project example, CC BY-SA 4.0. Uses spd-checker.py selected in Quarto. -->
<quiz><question type="stack">
<name><text>A symmetric positive definite matrix</text></name>
<questionvariables><text></text></questionvariables>
<questionsimplify>1</questionsimplify>
<questiontext format="html"><text><![CDATA[<p>Give any symmetric positive definite \(2\times2\) matrix. Use integers or exact fractions.</p><p>[[input:ansm]] [[validation:ansm]] [[feedback:result]]</p>]]></text></questiontext>
